covers: Hand recipe (kind repro-steps) for SX-ORC-09, authored by muse-b2 as author of record (CB-0823 ORC subgroup) from the fixer's supplied content: /Users/dutch/.zuko/quality/SX-ORC-09.check.md (seat B3, branch sx/core-loop, build f2ed241fb, branch head 3d4eac156 after the riding ORC-13 doc repair). Value-assertion provenance: INDEPENDENT — both reference cases are hand-computed in the check file from cited public sources (Gillespie, Fundamentals of Vehicle Dynamics, for the tyre-friction bound a <= mu*g; the Anderson Breguet-electric form and the orc.mass-bom envelope for the drone case), not from the solver's own output. Founder ruling executed (F10, answered by Ramaj first-hand 2026-11-18, dossier 680): the user's stated priorities govern when given (must / at least / ideally, from an explicit priority field or the requirement's own source words); otherwise min-max relative change; the min-max version first plus up to two Pareto alternatives, each relaxing a different requirement, all fully computed and each verified against ALL declared constraints before it ships; every change cites the solver envelope that forced it; per CB-0835 rule 2 the answer ships with its envelope, worded 'closest within the stated envelope'; never refuse, never invent a number. Behaviour: orc.realistic-fallback (v1.0.0, L3) solves the declared constraint model exactly at the JS tier — per-metric limit constraints and pairwise ratio constraints, each carrying its forcing envelope ({solver, citation}) as data; limits compose exactly, a violated ratio is solved in closed form (the priority-held single-side relaxation when priorities differ and it verifies, else the balanced min-max). Outputs carry verdict (relaxed / feasible-as-requested), the claim, requested point with resolved priorities, realistic point, changes[] with forcedBy citations, alternatives[], maxRelativeChange, and the envelope block. Named-not-claimed dependencies: the general OPT over arbitrary solver constraints is the SXE-21 engine tier — declared engineDependent [sxe-21] and reported NOT_COMPUTED engine_unavailable:sxe-21 in every result's envelope block and warnings; the JS result is never labelled as the engine result; a constraint interaction the closed forms cannot compose into a verified feasible point returns NOT_COMPUTED engine_tier_required:sxe-21, and contradictory limit envelopes return NOT_COMPUTED contradictory_envelopes naming both citations. SXC-26 wiring rides in the same landing: chain-run's permanent F10 skip is retired — the declared fallback link runs on infeasible chains (in place on a stopped link, after the seams on a violated seam, inserted before the report link) and NEVER signs the original request (an over-budget chain still receipts SEAM_VIOLATION, a stopped chain still receipts INCOMPLETE); undeclared fallback -> SKIPPED 'not declared in the chain input (optional link)'; declared on a feasible chain -> SKIPPED 'chain feasible as requested'. Whether SXC-26's already-registered recipe needs re-registration for the declaration-layer change is its author of record's (B6) call, flagged by the fixer — not part of this registration. Hygiene legs ride from the fixer's suite: inputs echo exactly (SC-05; structured echo asserted in-suite, the shared helper's echo leg being scalar-only), a bound without its declared unit is refused (SC-04), nothing is defaulted (SC-03), and the declaration-hygiene probe holds (rankSolvers 'mass properties' still tops at cad.mass-properties-brep). Reviewer: at activation, confirm the discriminator transcript below still fails against the pinned pre-fix instance and bind packet_id.
discriminator: Pre-fix transcript (from SX-ORC-09.check.md, replayed against the parent commit 6e113883b on sx/core-loop): orc.realistic-fallback is absent from the registry — listSolvers() carries 143 entries and getSolver('orc.realistic-fallback') returns undefined; the chain's fallback step is a permanent skip naming F10; every reference-case test fails at the import of the missing module. Post-fix: 144 registry entries, the solver computes both reference cases to the hand-computed values in the steps below, and the chain runs the fallback link on infeasible chains. Fixer regression at the tested tree: affected suites 72/72, full stack set 287/287.
steps: Via MCP conkay_solve {solver_id: "orc.realistic-fallback", typed inputs from docs/conkay/solvers/orc.realistic-fallback.md's replay request} — reference case 1 ('0-100 km/h in 0.5 s' vs the tyre-friction bound a <= mu*g, mu = 1.0 declared, g = 9.80665): expect verdict relaxed, claim 'closest within the stated envelope', the balanced min-max point at speed 8.3353045 m/s (30.0071 km/h) and time 0.8499645 s with ratio exactly 9.80665, every change citing the friction envelope, and two Pareto alternatives — speed alone at 4.903325 m/s (relative change 0.8234803) and time alone at 2.8325450 s (relative change 4.6650901). The envelope block reports NOT_COMPUTED engine_unavailable:sxe-21 for the general OPT leg; the JS-tier point is never labelled as the engine result.

Reference case 2 ('1 kg drone carrying 100 kg for 10 h' vs the mass-closure ratio payload/totalMass <= 0.40 and the energy endurance limit), with totalMass ranked 'must' by explicit field: expect the primary to hold totalMass at 1 kg, payload relaxed alone to exactly 0.4 kg (relative change 0.996), endurance relaxed to the limit (relative change 0.4289589); alternatives include the min-max balance (payload 0.7968127 kg, totalMass 1.9920319 kg, the must-relaxation flagged) and mass alone (250 kg). Repeat without the ranking: the balance leads, maxRelativeChange 0.9920319. Repeat with the ranking carried in source words ('the drone must mass 1 kg'): the ranking resolves identically.
Feasible leg: a request inside every declared envelope — expect verdict feasible-as-requested with no changes and no alternatives.

Adversarial: a bound stated as a bare number without its declared unit — expect refusal (SC-04). A constraint carrying no citation — expect refusal. Two contradictory limit envelopes on one metric — expect NOT_COMPUTED contradictory_envelopes naming both citations. A constraint interaction the closed forms cannot compose into a verified feasible point — expect NOT_COMPUTED engine_tier_required:sxe-21, never an improvised number.

Chain leg (SXC-26 wiring): run the golden chain infeasible with a declared fallback — expect the fallback link to run (in place on a stopped link, after the seams on a violated seam, before the report link), its result in outputs.fallback, and the receipt to still sign the original failure (SEAM_VIOLATION or INCOMPLETE) — the fallback never signs the original request. Repeat with no fallback declared — expect SKIPPED 'not declared in the chain input (optional link)'. Repeat declared on a feasible chain — expect SKIPPED 'chain feasible as requested — the declared fallback was not needed'.
title: orc.realistic-fallback: an infeasible request returns the closest point within the stated envelope — priorities first, min-max presented first, every change citing its forcing envelope
